# Providers

Mayon talks to AI models through configurable providers. Each provider is an adapter that implements a common streaming interface. The app ships with templates for popular providers and supports any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

## Provider templates

Clicking **Add provider** in Settings opens a picker with eighteen built-in templates, listed below in the order they appear. No template is a default — **DeepSeek** simply leads the list. Each template prefills a base URL and a starter model list, and you can edit the base URL before saving.

| Template | Type | Prefilled base URL | API key |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek | OpenAI-compatible | `https://api.deepseek.com` | Required |
| xAI (Grok) | OpenAI-compatible | `https://api.x.ai/v1` | Required |
| Moonshot Kimi | OpenAI-compatible | `https://api.moonshot.ai/v1` | Required |
| Qwen (DashScope) | OpenAI-compatible | `https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` | Required |
| Groq | OpenAI-compatible | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | Required |
| Mistral | OpenAI-compatible | `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` | Required |
| OpenCode Zen | OpenAI-compatible | `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1` | Required |
| LiteLLM (self-hosted) | OpenAI-compatible | `http://localhost:4000` | Only if your proxy enforces one |
| Vercel AI Gateway | OpenAI-compatible | `https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1` | Required |
| Requesty | OpenAI-compatible | `https://router.requesty.ai/v1` | Required |
| Z.AI (GLM) | OpenAI-compatible | `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4` | Required |
| Kilo Gateway | OpenAI-compatible | `https://api.kilo.ai/api/gateway` | Required |
| OpenRouter | OpenAI-compatible | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | Required |
| OpenAI | OpenAI-compatible | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | Required |
| Anthropic (Claude) | Anthropic | `https://api.anthropic.com` | Required |
| Google Gemini | Gemini | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` | Required |
| Ollama (local) | Ollama | `http://localhost:11434/api` | Not required |
| GitHub Copilot | GitHub Copilot | `https://api.githubcopilot.com` | GitHub sign-in instead |

Most templates discover their model catalog automatically: Mayon fetches the provider's live model list and offers a searchable model picker. The templates that ship a fixed starter model list instead are Qwen (DashScope), OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini, and Ollama (local).

**GitHub Copilot** works differently from the other templates: instead of pasting an API key, you connect your GitHub account. Click **Connect GitHub account** in the provider's settings and authorize Mayon in the browser — there is no key to copy or paste. This sign-in flow is handled by the Mayon server, so the server must be running. Once connected, the provider shows the connected account, and a **Reconnect** action appears if the authorization ever expires.

## Configuring a provider

1. Open **Settings** (gear icon in the sidebar).
2. Click **Add provider**.
3. Pick a template from the list.
4. Edit the **base URL** if needed (e.g., point to a self-hosted instance).
5. Select or search for a **model**. Templates with automatic discovery fetch the provider's live catalog and offer a searchable model picker; the others offer a fixed starter list.
6. Paste your **API key** and click **Save key**. The LiteLLM (self-hosted) and Ollama (local) templates need no key. For GitHub Copilot, skip this step and use **Connect GitHub account** as described above.
7. Click **Set active**.

After saving, the provider becomes available for new chats. Reload the tab to confirm the configuration persists.

## Switching providers

Add multiple providers and switch between them using the "Set active" action. The active provider is used for new chats and streaming. You can switch at any time — existing chats retain the provider and model they were created with.

## Key storage

API keys are never stored in the settings database. The `settings` table holds only non-secret provider configuration fields (base URL, default model, template type).

**Browser:** Keys are stored in IndexedDB under the same origin as the app. The key is not sent to any server other than the provider's API endpoint during streaming (or the Mayon server's CORS proxy, which is same-origin and transient). The settings screen shows an **API key (stored locally)** field, which becomes **Replace API key (stored locally)** once a key is saved — the stored key itself is never displayed.

## CORS limitation in the browser

Some providers (notably Anthropic) block direct `fetch` requests from browser origins. When this happens, the chat view shows a clear "Start the Mayon server (`docker compose up`) for CORS-free access" notice instead of a raw error. When the server is connected with the `llm-proxy` cap, requests to CORS-blocked providers route through the server's CORS proxy.

OpenAI-compatible gateways (OpenRouter, Kilo Gateway, Z.AI) generally allow browser requests. If you do not have the server running, stick to these providers or use Ollama for local models.
